newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Slovenia, Romania creep closer to NATO club.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia, Romania creep closer to NATO club.

text.p: Slovenia and Romania have emerged as strong candidates to clinch NATO membership next July along with favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, NATO sources said on Thursday.
"Nothing is yet decided, but the trend is clearly that way," said one senior official.
NATO's 16 current members are set to invite a handful of countries from former communist East Europe to join the alliance at a special summit in Madrid on July 8-9.

France has strongly pushed for both Romania and Slovenia to be admitted in the first wave, but some other countries, notably the powerful northern European states and the United States, are believed to be lukewarm on the idea.
NATO insiders say taking in five more members would make the alliance unwieldy and leave other applicant countries, such as the Baltic States and Bulgaria, feeling aggrieved.

Some U.S. administration officials however favour granting Slovenia membership as a way of rewarding it for staying free of the worst of the fighting which accompanied the break up of former Yugoslavia.
"Washington realises some concessions may have to be made to the southern states and as a result Romania could really squeeze in," said one NATO diplomat.
